name: Advocate Naveen Singla
bio: Naveen Singla founded the practice in 1997, the year of his enrolment, with a straightforward conviction: clients are better served by candour than by optimism. That principle still governs how the firm takes instructions — every matter opens with an honest assessment of merits, even where the answer is that litigation is the wrong route.

He appears regularly before the High Court and appellate tribunals in civil, constitutional and arbitration matters, and has led the firm's most complex property and commercial disputes. He is also the partner clients reach when a matter has gone wrong elsewhere and needs to be rebuilt from the pleadings up.
imageAlt: Portrait of Advocate Naveen Singla, Founder

name: Advocate Ria Goyal
bio: Advocate Ria Goyal leads the corporate and taxation practice. A dual qualification in law and company secretaryship shapes the approach: transactions are structured with the compliance and tax consequences already accounted for, rather than discovered at filing.

The practice covers founders and family businesses through investment rounds, restructurings and successions, together with representation in scrutiny assessments and appeals before the Tribunal. It also carries the firm's SARFAESI and insolvency mandates on both the lender and borrower side.
imageAlt: Portrait of Advocate Ria Goyal, Senior Partner

name: Advocate Kushal Kumar
bio: Advocate Kushal Kumar heads the family and matrimonial practice and is an accredited mediator. A substantial proportion of the caseload here is resolved through negotiated settlement, which in family matters usually serves the client — and any children involved — far better than a contested judgment.

Where a matter must be litigated it is conducted firmly, with particular experience in custody, maintenance and NRI matrimonial disputes. Clients consistently describe these consultations as the first time the process was explained to them clearly.
